questions.title: Prejunctional alpha2 activation inhibits noradrenaline release
questions.question: Activation of prejunctional α2 receptors on sympathetic nerve endings is associated with:

explanations.A: Correct. Noradrenaline released at the terminal acts back on its own prejunctional alpha2 autoreceptors. This Gi-coupled activation inhibits further noradrenaline (NEP) release, a negative-feedback loop that limits how much transmitter a single nerve impulse releases.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Increased IP3 and DAG is a Gq-coupled signalling pattern, such as that of postsynaptic alpha1 receptors, not the Gi-coupled presynaptic alpha2 autoreceptor.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Alpha2 autoreceptor activation inhibits, rather than stimulates, further noradrenaline release -- it does not stimulate its synthesis either.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The prejunctional alpha2 autoreceptor's feedback effect is on noradrenaline release at the sympathetic terminal itself, not specifically or exclusively on serotonin (5-HT) release.

questions.learning_objective: State that prejunctional alpha2 receptor activation inhibits further noradrenaline release.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Inhibition of NEP release"

questions.title: Heart failure is not a standard epinephrine indication
questions.question: Epinephrine is used in the treatment of all the following conditions EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cardiac arrest is a genuine epinephrine indication -- its alpha1-mediated vasoconstriction improves coronary and cerebral perfusion pressure during resuscitation.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Anaphylactic shock is a core epinephrine indication, reversing bronchospasm and hypotension through its combined alpha/beta effects.
explanations.C: Correct. Heart failure is not a standard epinephrine indication. Despite epinephrine's inotropic and chronotropic effects, its arrhythmogenic potential and alpha-mediated increase in afterload outweigh any short-term inotropic benefit in this chronic setting, so it is the one condition on this list epinephrine is not used to treat.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Complete heart block is a genuine epinephrine indication, used to increase heart rate when the normal conduction pathway has failed.

questions.learning_objective: State that heart failure is not a standard epinephrine indication, unlike cardiac arrest, anaphylactic shock and complete heart block.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Heart failure"

questions.title: Norepinephrine is given by IV infusion only
questions.question: Norepinephrine is used by:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Norepinephrine's severe local vasoconstrictive potency makes subcutaneous injection a tissue-necrosis risk, ruling out this route.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Norepinephrine is inactivated by first-pass gut and liver metabolism, so it is not effective by the oral route.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Like the SC route, intramuscular injection risks severe local vasoconstriction and tissue damage, ruling it out for norepinephrine.
explanations.D: Correct. Norepinephrine is used only by IV infusion. This route avoids the local tissue-necrosis risk of SC or IM injection and the first-pass inactivation of oral dosing, while allowing the careful, continuous titration a potent vasopressor needs.

questions.learning_objective: State that norepinephrine is administered only by IV infusion.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: I.V. infusion route"

questions.title: Noradrenaline is agonist at alpha1, alpha2, beta1 but not beta2
questions.question: The following sympathomimetic amine has agonistic action on alpha1 + alpha 2+ beta 1 + beta 3 adrenoceptors, but not on beta 2 receptors:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Isoprenaline is essentially beta-selective (beta1 and beta2), with negligible alpha activity -- the opposite emphasis from the profile described here.
explanations.B: Correct. Noradrenaline is an agonist at alpha1, alpha2, beta1 and beta3 adrenoceptors, but has negligible activity at beta2. This selective sparing of beta2 is what distinguishes its receptor profile from adrenaline's, which activates all four classic subtypes including beta2.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Adrenaline is an agonist at all four classic adrenoceptor subtypes -- alpha1, alpha2, beta1 and beta2 -- so it does not spare beta2 the way this question describes.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Phenylephrine is a selective alpha1 agonist with essentially no beta activity at all, not the alpha1/alpha2/beta1/beta3-without-beta2 profile described here.

questions.learning_objective: State noradrenaline's receptor-selectivity profile (alpha1, alpha2, beta1, not beta2), contrasted with adrenaline, isoprenaline and phenylephrine.

questions.title: Axonal reuptake terminates noradrenaline's action
questions.question: The principal process which terminates the action of noradrenaline released from adrenergic nerve ending is:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Extraneuronal uptake (Uptake-2) contributes to noradrenaline clearance but is a secondary route, not the principal termination mechanism.
explanations.B: Correct. Axonal (neuronal) uptake back into the presynaptic terminal -- often called Uptake-1 -- is the principal process terminating noradrenaline's synaptic action. It is quantitatively dominant over extraneuronal uptake, COMT methylation and MAO degradation, all of which play only secondary roles.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Methylation by COMT is a real but secondary metabolic route for noradrenaline, largely extraneuronal, not the principal termination mechanism.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Degradation by MAO occurs mainly intraneuronally on noradrenaline that has escaped storage vesicles, a secondary rather than the principal clearance route.

questions.learning_objective: State that axonal (neuronal) reuptake is the principal process terminating noradrenaline's synaptic action.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Axonal uptake"

questions.title: Ephedrine is a noncatecholamine sympathomimetic
questions.question: Which of the following is a noncatecholamine sympathomimetic:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Adrenaline is a true catecholamine, carrying the catechol ring structure -- it is not the noncatecholamine option here.
explanations.B: Correct. Ephedrine lacks the catechol (dihydroxybenzene) ring structure that defines a true catecholamine, making it a noncatecholamine sympathomimetic. This structural difference is part of why ephedrine, unlike the catecholamines, survives oral administration.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Dopamine is a catecholamine (the direct biosynthetic precursor of noradrenaline), not the noncatecholamine sympathomimetic described here.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Isoprenaline is a synthetic catecholamine derivative, carrying the catechol ring, not a noncatecholamine sympathomimetic.

questions.learning_objective: Identify ephedrine as a noncatecholamine sympathomimetic, distinct from adrenaline, dopamine and isoprenaline.

questions.title: Sympathetic postganglionic fibres are adrenergic
questions.question: Which one of the following sites is characterized by adrenergic transmission?

options.A: Synaptic fibers in the eccrine gland
options.C: Sympathetic fibers in the adrenal medulla

explanations.A: Incorrect. Sympathetic fibres to eccrine (thermoregulatory sweat) glands are an anatomical exception -- although sympathetic, they release acetylcholine (cholinergic), not noradrenaline.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Parasympathetic preganglionic fibres are cholinergic, acting on nicotinic receptors at the parasympathetic ganglion, not adrenergic.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The sympathetic fibres innervating the adrenal medulla are themselves preganglionic and cholinergic, even though the medulla they stimulate secretes catecholamines into the blood as a hormone rather than releasing them as a synaptic neurotransmitter.
explanations.D: Correct. Adrenergic transmission -- release of noradrenaline as the neurotransmitter -- is the property of sympathetic postganglionic fibres. This is the site classically described as adrenergic, distinguishing it from the cholinergic exceptions among the other options.

questions.learning_objective: Identify sympathetic postganglionic fibres as the site of adrenergic transmission, distinct from cholinergic exceptions.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Sympathetic postganglionic fibers"
